faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Is a lease takeover legal in Poland?
faq.a1: Yes. A lease takeover (cesja najmu) is a standard legal instrument under Polish civil law. It requires the consent of all parties: the current tenant, the new tenant, and the landlord. Passflat helps you find the match — the legal transfer is between you and the landlord.
faq.q2: What exactly is a lease takeover?
faq.a2: A lease takeover is an amendment to an existing lease agreement where the current tenant transfers their rights and obligations to a new tenant. The terms of the original agreement (rent, period, etc.) typically remain unchanged. The landlord must consent.
faq.q3: Do I need the landlord's consent?
faq.a3: Yes. The landlord must agree to the lease transfer. Most landlords agree because they gain a reliable tenant and avoid vacancy. It's in everyone's interest.
faq.a4: Listing is free. Optional promoted listings (for better visibility) are available for a small fee starting at 39 PLN. Browsing and cost reports are completely free.
faq.a5: We're starting with Warsaw, but the platform is designed for multi-city expansion. Kraków, Wrocław, and other European cities are on our roadmap.

about.title: About Passflat
about.subtitle: We're making renting in Poland transparent, fair, and community-driven.

problem.label: The Problem
problem.title: Renting in Poland is broken
problem.p1: Tenants lose deposits when they need to move before the lease ends. There's no easy way to find a replacement — so you either pay a penalty or lose months of rent.
problem.p2: Utility costs are hidden until you sign the lease. You find out about real monthly expenses after moving in — and by then it's too late.
problem.p3: Agency fees are steep, and foreigners face an even bigger information gap when searching for apartments.

solution.label: Our Solution
solution.title: A complete rental toolkit built by the community
solution.pillar1Desc: Find a replacement and keep your deposit. Take over someone's lease and skip the agency fee. Lease assignment is a standard legal instrument in Poland — we make it easy.
solution.pillar2Desc: Find a compatible roommate or fill a vacant room. Specify preferences, room type, and per-person costs — so both sides know what to expect.
solution.pillar3Desc: Sublet your apartment for a fixed period while you're away. Set exact dates, total price, and house rules — all in one listing.
solution.pillar4Desc: Community-sourced real utility costs. Know exactly what you'll pay for electricity, gas, heating, and water before you sign.

team.title: Built by renters, for renters
team.description: We're a small team based in Warsaw. We rent here ourselves and know the pain firsthand — lost deposits, surprise utility bills, and a frustratingly opaque rental market. We built Passflat because we needed it ourselves.

general.title: General
general.a1: Passflat is a rental marketplace specializing in lease takeovers in Warsaw. It also features a cost transparency database so you can see real utility costs before signing a lease.
general.a2: Yes. Browsing listings, cost reports, and posting listings are free. We offer optional promoted listings for better visibility, starting at 39 PLN.
general.q3: What cities does Passflat operate in?
general.a3: Currently we operate in Warsaw. Expansion to Kraków, Wrocław, and other European cities is on our roadmap.
general.a4: Passflat is available in Polish, English, Russian, and Ukrainian — reflecting Warsaw's diverse tenant community.

leaseTakeovers.title: Lease Takeovers
leaseTakeovers.a1: A lease takeover is an amendment to a lease agreement where the current tenant transfers their rights and obligations to a new tenant. The terms of the original agreement typically remain unchanged. The landlord must consent to the transfer.
leaseTakeovers.q2: Is a lease takeover legal in Poland?
leaseTakeovers.a2: Yes. A lease takeover is a standard legal instrument under Polish civil law. It requires consent from three parties: the current tenant, the new tenant, and the landlord.
leaseTakeovers.q3: Do I need the landlord's consent?
leaseTakeovers.a3: Yes, the landlord must agree. Most landlords consent because they retain a reliable tenant and avoid vacancy — it's in everyone's interest.
leaseTakeovers.q4: How do I create a listing?
leaseTakeovers.a4: Log in, click "Create Listing" and fill in the address, apartment details, photos, and cost breakdown. Your listing will appear on the map and in search results after publishing.
leaseTakeovers.q5: How long does a listing stay active?
leaseTakeovers.a5: Listings are active for 60 days. You can renew or close them at any time from your dashboard.
leaseTakeovers.a6: Yes. Promoted listings appear at the top of search results for 7, 14, or 30 days. Prices start at 39 PLN.

costTransparency.title: Cost Transparency
costTransparency.q1: How does the cost database work?
costTransparency.a1: Tenants submit anonymous cost reports for their buildings — including rent, admin fee, electricity, gas, heating, water, and internet. Data is aggregated and displayed per building so future tenants can see what they'll actually pay.
costTransparency.q2: Why do I need to submit my costs to unlock data?
costTransparency.a2: The database is community-powered. By submitting your data, you help others and unlock full access to reports for all buildings. It's a fair exchange that keeps the database growing.
costTransparency.a3: Yes. Your apartment number is never displayed publicly. Cost data is shown in aggregated form (averages, min/max per building), so individual submissions cannot be identified.
costTransparency.a4: Report your monthly rent, admin fee, and utility costs: electricity, gas, heating, water, and internet. The more complete the report, the more useful it is for the community.

account.title: Account & Privacy
account.q1: How do I create an account?
account.a1: Click "Sign up" and register with email or a Google account. You'll receive a confirmation email to verify your address.
account.q2: How do I delete my account?
account.a2: Contact us at contact@passflat.eu and we'll process your account deletion request. Your listings will be removed and personal data erased in accordance with GDPR.
account.q3: How is my personal data used?
account.a3: We use your data solely to provide the service — managing listings, sending notifications, and displaying anonymized cost reports. We never sell personal data. See our Privacy Policy for details.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: How Passflat collects, uses, and protects your personal data.

intro.title: Introduction
intro.p1: Passflat ("we", "us", "our") is a rental marketplace platform operated from Warsaw, Poland. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, store, and protect your personal data when you use our website and services at passflat.eu.
intro.p2: We are committed to protecting your privacy in compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable Polish data protection laws. By using Passflat, you acknowledge that you have read and understood this policy.

dataCollected.title: Data We Collect
dataCollected.intro: We collect only the data necessary to provide and improve our services:

account.title: Account Data
account.item1: Email address and display name (via email or Google OAuth registration through Supabase Auth)

listings.title: Listing Data
listings.item1: Apartment address (street, building number, district, postal code)
listings.item3: Cost breakdown (rent, admin fee, estimated utilities) and apartment details (area, rooms, amenities, description)

costReports.title: Cost Report Data
costReports.item2: Monthly utility costs (electricity, gas, heating, water, internet) — displayed only in aggregated form

usage.title: Usage & Technical Data
usage.item1: Pages visited, interactions, and feature usage (collected via PostHog analytics)
usage.item2: IP address, browser type, device information, and operating system (standard server logs)

howWeUse.title: How We Use Your Data
howWeUse.item1: Providing the service: displaying listings, connecting tenants, showing cost reports
howWeUse.item2: Sending notifications: email alerts when someone expresses interest in your listing (via Resend)
howWeUse.item3: Improving the platform: understanding usage patterns, fixing bugs, developing new features
howWeUse.item4: Ensuring security: preventing fraud, abuse, and unauthorized access
howWeUse.noSell: We do NOT sell your personal data to third parties. Ever.

dataSharing.title: Data Sharing
dataSharing.intro: We share data only in the following, limited circumstances:
dataSharing.item1: Cost reports are displayed in aggregated, anonymized form — apartment numbers are never shown publicly
dataSharing.item2: Listing contact details are shared only with users who express interest through the platform

processors.title: Data Processors
processors.vercel: Vercel — website hosting and serverless functions
processors.stripe: Stripe — payment processing for promoted listings
processors.google: Google Places API — address autocomplete (address data only)
processors.mapbox: Mapbox — map rendering (no personal data shared)

retention.title: Data Retention
retention.account: Account data: retained until you delete your account
retention.listings: Listings: active for 60 days, then archived for 30 days before deletion
retention.costReports: Cost reports: retained indefinitely in anonymized, aggregated form to maintain the community database

rights.title: Your Rights (GDPR)
rights.intro: Under the General Data Protection Regulation, you have the following rights:
rights.access: Right of access — request a copy of the personal data we hold about you
rights.rectification: Right to rectification — correct inaccurate or incomplete data
rights.erasure: Right to erasure — request deletion of your personal data ("right to be forgotten")
rights.portability: Right to data portability — receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format
rights.objection: Right to object — object to processing based on legitimate interest
rights.withdrawConsent: Right to withdraw consent — withdraw consent at any time where processing is based on consent
rights.howToExercise: To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@passflat.eu. We will respond within 30 days as required by GDPR.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.intro: We use a minimal set of cookies:
cookies.essential: Essential cookies: authentication session tokens (required for the service to work)
cookies.analytics: Analytics cookies: PostHog (optional — you can opt out via browser settings or our cookie banner)

contact.title: Data Contact
contact.text: For privacy questions or to exercise your GDPR rights, contact our data protection team:

changes.title: Changes to This Policy
changes.text: We may update this Privacy Policy to reflect changes in our practices or legal requirements. We will notify registered users of significant changes via email. The "Last updated" date at the top of this page indicates when the policy was last revised.

termsPage.title: Terms of Service
termsPage.subtitle: Rules and guidelines for using the Passflat platform.

acceptance.title: 1. Acceptance of Terms
acceptance.p1: By using Passflat (passflat.eu), you agree to these Terms of Service. If you do not agree, please do not use the platform.
acceptance.p2: These terms apply to all users of the platform, including tenants listing apartments, tenants searching for apartments, and users submitting cost reports.

service.title: 2. Service Description
service.item1: Passflat is a platform connecting tenants for lease takeovers — helping current tenants find replacements and new tenants find apartments.
service.item2: Passflat provides a community-sourced cost database where tenants share real utility costs to help others make informed decisions.
service.item3: Passflat is NOT a real estate agency, property manager, or party to any lease agreement. We facilitate connections between tenants — any legal arrangements are between the involved parties.

accounts.title: 3. User Accounts
accounts.item1: You must be at least 18 years old to create an account and use Passflat.
accounts.item2: You may only create one account. Duplicate accounts may be removed.
accounts.item3: You are responsible for the security of your login credentials and for all activity on your account.
accounts.item4: We reserve the right to suspend or delete accounts that violate these terms or engage in abusive behavior.

listingRules.title: 4. Listing Rules
listingRules.intro: When posting a listing on Passflat, you agree to the following:
listingRules.item1: Listings must be for real, currently available apartments that you have the right to offer for lease takeover.
listingRules.item2: You must be the current tenant of the apartment or have explicit authorization from the tenant to post the listing.
listingRules.item3: Cost information (rent, admin fee, utilities) must be accurate and reflect actual monthly expenses.
listingRules.item4: Listings must not contain discriminatory, misleading, offensive, or illegal content.
listingRules.item5: Passflat reserves the right to remove any listing that violates these rules without prior notice.
listingRules.item6: Listings expire automatically after 60 days. You can renew or close them at any time from your dashboard.

costReports.title: 5. Cost Reports
costReports.item1: Cost reports must reflect real costs from your personal experience as a tenant in the reported building.
costReports.item2: Submitting false or deliberately misleading cost data may result in account removal and deletion of all reports.
costReports.item3: Cost reports are displayed in anonymized, aggregated form. Apartment numbers are never published.

payments.title: 6. Payments
payments.p1: Promoted listings are a paid feature that boosts listing visibility in search results. Payments are securely processed via Stripe. Prices are in PLN and include taxes.
payments.p2: Refunds for promoted listings are handled on a case-by-case basis. Contact us at legal@passflat.eu for refund requests.

liability.title: 7. Limitation of Liability
liability.item1: Passflat is a marketplace platform. We do not verify apartments, conduct property inspections, or guarantee the accuracy of user-submitted information.
liability.item2: Users are solely responsible for verifying listing information, conducting viewings, and entering into legal agreements (amendments, lease assignments) with landlords and other tenants.
liability.item3: Passflat is not liable for any disputes, losses, or damages arising from transactions or interactions between users or between users and landlords.

ip.title: 8. Intellectual Property
ip.p1: The Passflat platform, including its design, code, branding, and content (excluding user-generated content), is the intellectual property of Passflat.
ip.p2: By posting content on Passflat (listings, photos, cost reports), you grant us a non-exclusive, worldwide license to display and distribute that content on the platform for the purpose of providing the service.

law.title: 9. Governing Law
law.text: These Terms of Service are governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Republic of Poland. Any disputes arising from these terms shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Warsaw.
